national_raw_news.content: The First BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting concluded in New Delhi with the adoption of the Delhi Declaration. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC Nations have strongly condemned terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism. In the declaration, the BIMSTEC nations reiterated their determination to prevent, combat and eliminate terrorism and violent extremism conducive to terrorism in a comprehensive and sustained manner, in accordance with the UN Charter and international law. They also reaffirmed commitment to strengthening regional cooperation under BIMSTEC for realizing a connected, secure, resilient, developed and prosperous BIMSTEC region. They also expressed deepest condolences and solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks in Member States and their families and with the Governments of the affected States. The nations called for those responsible to be brought to justice in accordance with applicable domestic and international law. The Delhi Declaration also called for effective implementation of the finalized Plans of Action in areas of Human Trafficking, Narcotic Drugs and Precursor Chemicals and Anti-Money Laundering, as well as finalisation of the Plan of Action by the Sub-Group on Cooperation in Countering Radicalization and Terrorism. It also called for effective implementation of the BIMSTEC Convention on Mutual Legal Assistance in Criminal Matters, which was signed in March 2022 at the 5th BIMSTEC Summit in Colombo. The BIMSTEC nations also reaffirmed the principle that cooperation within BIMSTEC in the security sector is based on respect for the principle of sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, non-aggression, peaceful co-existence and mutual respect.

national_raw_news.title: 5 mins ago | National 68 EAM S Jaishankar says India-US trade talks heading in right direction
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that India-US trade talks are heading in the right direction and a deal is being ironed out currently. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Dr Jaishankar informed that trade ministers of the two countries are working on it and both nations are pretty far advanced in the process of negotiations for the trade deal. Replying to a query, Dr Jaishankar emphasised that the US has repositioned itself and every country has to recalibrate and reset its relationship with the US. He highlighted that India has a strong Strategic Partnership with the US. In China, the External Affairs Minister maintained that the bilateral relationship will have consequences if peace and tranquillity in border areas are disturbed. He stated that the relationship is moving towards normalcy as the border areas are settling down. He noted that India and China have been able to restore peace and tranquillity in border areas. Dr Jaishankar remarked that the trade balance between India and China is completely tilted and is extremely one-sided. He said India is not getting a level playing field in China. Replying to another query on Russia, Dr Jaishankar clearly pointed out that India has never encountered a whiff of a suggestion that anything India is procuring from Russia comes with Chinese tech. He opined that because of the Ukraine war, Russia has turned much more to Asia. He said that it is in India’s interest, and the world’s interest, that Russia has multiple choices. He said India is a natural option in that regard.

national_raw_news.title: 8 mins ago | International 8 US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation &...
national_raw_news.content: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week to strengthen energy cooperation and strategic partnership between the two countries. US State Department said, Mr Rubio will travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar during his tour. State Department said, he will meet with senior government officials to strengthen India-US strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Mr Rubio will also meet business leaders to promote investment and economic cooperation. This will be Mr Rubio’s second visit to India since May, when he attended the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting hosted by External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi. Before arriving in India, Mr Rubio will participate in the C5+1 Ministerial meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The meeting will focus on how strategic cooperation through the diplomatic platform can promote a more peaceful and prosperous future for the US and Central Asian countries. Mr Rubio will also hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from the five Central Asian countries – Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. A US commercial delegation comprising more than 200 business leaders will accompany Mr Rubio to promote stronger commercial cooperation between the US and Central Asia.
